text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000064 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but the small documented sample supports the billed level at a rate in line with peers.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern itself looks consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel: most 99215s fall on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and the 99215 share exceeds the all-provider rate in every complexity band. Sampled low-complexity examples are routine presentations such as back pain, rash, URI and follow-up codes (e.g., C0032149, C0031737, C0032123). The documentation does not confirm this, though: the documented 99215 unsupported rate matches the comparison providers. That sample is thin (17 charts) and may be inflated, since several notes claim moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test on the claim, and C0032261 (a 0-condition back-pain visit) is documented as high MDM with no time recorded. A reviewer should first pull charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with C0032261 and the supported examples lacking minutes, to check whether MDM narratives are templated or cloned and whether the data reviewed matches orders or results actually on file."}
